# Introducing Specs: Markdown as a medium

Luke ZhangProduct Manager, Figma

Johnny DallasSoftware Engineer, Figma

Aosheng RanProduct Designer, Figma

 Inside Figma
 Product updates
 Config
 News

We’re launching Specs, a container for your context that lives on the Figma canvas.

## Share Introducing Specs: Markdown as a medium

Turn existing Markdown into a spec by dragging and dropping any .md file onto the canvas. [...] Today, more and more product builders are working in Markdown, as collaborating with agents becomes more standard. It’s the de facto format for sharing context. But for all the context Markdown helps us express, it’s missing a lot of context, too. Markdown files tend to be single player on local computers, with brittle relationships to each other, and little tying them to the projects that spawned them. While most context is ephemeral, some context evolves into key inputs that need refinement over time and collaboration. That’s why we built Specs: a multiplayer container that allows context to fully express itself and move into, out of, and across Figma. [...] Connectors help bring outside context into Specs too. If you’re drafting a technical spec, for example, you can pull in context directly from your codebase with the GitHub connector. Or, say your team uses Hex for product usage data, and your PRD has an open question that data could answer. Select the question, add the Hex connector, and ask the agent to run the analysis and leave its findings as a comment on the spec. The answer lands in the document, right where the question was asked.

You can also drag in content from the Figma canvas, like a design exploration you riffed on with your team, or a diagram of a proposed user flow. Then, when you drag it back out, you can still preserve Figma properties.
